bodies.text:
Noctalia-CI left a comment (noctalia-dev/umbriel#288)

## AI-generated triage analysis

This analysis reflects the date and source revision recorded below; it has not been reverified for this migration and is not a new maintainer verdict. Later discussion or fixes may supersede its findings and suggested next actions.

### AI analysis
Analyzed at (UTC): 2026-10-10T13:23:09+00:00
Source revision: 2026-09-21T14:44:16Z
Repository context: `21456686a8f21f82a0675cad658ffbeed35269b6` (checkout matched remote main at inventory).
Verification: discussion, source and implementation inspection only; no runtime reproduction performed.

#### Summary

Existing binds do not provide the requested pinned-window cycle behavior across a shared visible workspace.

#### Findings and evidence

The issue already supplies floating-focus and next-window binds. Pinned visibility can span a workspace different from the view’s home; current cycling filters home/workspace membership. [Focus handling](https://example.com/5eae3d6bd1a02ebcdac1d997c5bf129487215e9d88ff3209e1e21e3babc9bbd7c41df5c92fc2a7416cc69cf515) recognizes pins, while ID-specific focus is only a partial workaround and does not define cycle order. [INFERENCE] Visibility-based candidate selection and home-based selection differ, especially when several pinned floats share an output.

#### Suggested next action

Define pinned candidate visibility, ordering and floating/tiled cycle interaction. Use the supplied binds; do not ask again for them or substitute manual ID focus as complete coverage.

TOP RELEASE TO TRY

------------------------------------------------------
Use GitHub Copilot right from Slack or Microsoft Teams
------------------------------------------------------

Available in public preview, mention *@8404ca* in Slack or Microsoft Teams to put Copilot to work directly from your conversation. Note that this must be enabled by an administrator first. With the latest updates, Copilot can use even more context from your Slack or Teams conversations, including supported files, images, messages, and conversation history.

Useful if you want to:
----------------------

* Work with Copilot directly from Slack ( https://example.com/bbdd98e668a438bcddbd7f94b3fccb8a8f58b6b9472ddda9b92739a5020676918a5c0b3135b514331b45b5d57be19e4c0bbbe6cbbada807d9947dff01ee2ade167add2f79f535141727c53c1f9f8823e220322 ) or Microsoft Teams ( https://example.com/020907afa9ee459c43c28f0ca6655083988b51c2029feda3cf9b9671f6724b2cca4563eb3867b5eff045b8e98c52419a6b25bed8673b22bf1aabfc052e13f7e3769094471a880b2e79c47c3e964d762a3393af9d702f2de6398944 ).
* Give Copilot relevant context from your conversation.
* Avoid switching tools to get work started.

Explore Copilot in Slack and Microsoft Teams ( https://example.com/3f6bbc6b81a8196108d490964540c5242a3b89185c757de375a998d4ef482ef129b1a61e18418baf7bf05cd1ffe3a41ccb6b2cdc2dabf91f208f7d3a1592bc3a8f565398f9ae19a4f1b76414d03f9d6972fb8377dd1066ee061 )

COPILOT

-------------------------------------------
Let HydraFusion optimize your model choices
-------------------------------------------

HydraFusion coordinates multiple models behind the scenes, selecting the workflow that best balances performance, cost, and latency for every task. HydraFusion is currently available as a research preview for Copilot Business and Enterprise customers in Copilot CLI, Visual Studio Code, and the GitHub Copilot app.

See what HydraFusion has to offer ( https://example.com/27c1b564ffa0bbe18d8f38623668ed9ab99c9fa067c1ada1f68f635618da2396b57d8bb474b871adf619ca3d5dbce00c323615170ced23777fd43d526c35d579e03f6a90326d5753ad8520ea673563e33fc7586273f5c )

CLI UPDATE

--------------------------------------------------------
Attach media to issues and pull requests from GitHub CLI
--------------------------------------------------------

Add the *--attach* flag to commands that use Markdown text to include images or videos. You can even include alt text to describe the image. This lets you provide visual feedback directly without the need to switch tools.

Include some media in your CLI commands ( https://example.com/1fb68b09574af663d4d37b89c12a793d99d066e7df417ebac9fa527258758be30156d70380714618fef2dfd98d995c7a3ad04f947d107d429aa19924e4ebb3be5fb596bcdbf7e3b63029b6023eee901b850bfdd8d0c608c8e )

Explore the latest models and choose the options that best fit your organization’s needs.

Take advantage of a refreshed pull request listing page ( https://example.com/1c4d4c6fb1ad2488a1c462e7dbdc26ae712936ba56c18875084fdd693b37dad7117d50b337605a20f4681d7e62e3874aa3c57fe25b1a7c2683c334344bb52b3800f2491877d0ccf7d123c868c0281c005c642e714feb5608e89b6 )

Find and act on pull requests more easily with the refreshed repository-level pull request listing page. New filtering and contextual search options help you find what you need. This is in public preview.

Control available models at the global level ( https://example.com/787023870d9a546e16fe757ca6e631b375501b683627120f915f90ffbade83d7c787470bcf1971fdfc2b9ab043fba553a5ad327dd38a27bddeb02e6cf85b2a235aa46c429ad8115d7a1b0952ac4428abdeb )

Set a default model-availability policy for your organization or enterprise. Applicable models without an individual setting follow the global policy; existing model-specific settings remain unchanged.

Fine-tune GitHub Copilot’s auto model choices ( https://example.com/d3875963f3c2c5544d1b72d8a1fe99792d29b02cee88d6e80a3becc7d1fdb813634b8eedc29e7fbcafc753c7c69371915077666bde26f5170cf5a0b2fa06c06cecad56303db5700a103d36f938ed81129d5ad312860e7a4c967f2e )

Choose whether GitHub Copilot prioritizes efficiency, balance, or intelligence when using auto model selection. This helps you guide which models are selected while letting Copilot handle the specifics.

Have Copilot code review approve pull requests ( https://example.com/fc34fc3f2e84c4874f242c4f89e45a1a969f70749e7c8746036041f5c45fa7d13085dcb2f1b06d3a15c7b6ec047123d8af1e0293ae939d2a85c89847ac491fb352c122ea196f148a3d9375bab9a26de082b2d860692b7 )

By default, Copilot now provides an assessment of whether a pull request is ready to approve. Admins can also enable Copilot to submit approvals that count towards required approval rules.

Autofix findings from GitHub Code Quality ( https://example.com/d0bfbfebcc48964f86cd297ce0fab0822b8d28ec67752b419ba66977016ed142119b1a83b7b8deee7599b9161a84638fb30a5d2587caf4a91fcfd6fb14e1a0f7dd24689ccf6599eba5f6dcf0691b216ac58ecb87f323be46 )

Assign findings in your code quality backlog to Copilot in bulk, and it starts fixing them on a branch. When its work is done, Copilot opens a pull request for you to review and merge.

For a more detailed look, check out our latest Enterprise Roundup ( https://example.com/c215df3613c3ed4d2ba51852da16de577d5010c3073cc8342f1a5841dab8a8855000d3db908ac879ca9ec5f27b4190cbfc4 ).
